ground_truth.description: `claimRewards()` uses `IVoter.poolVote(veTokenId)` incorrectly; `poolVote` is a mapping, not a function returning an array, causing a revert.
ground_truth.root_cause: `claimRewards()` uses `IVoter.poolVote(veTokenId)` incorrectly; `poolVote` is a mapping, not a function returning an array, causing a revert.
ground_truth.attack_scenario: A test votes on pools, warps time, and `claimRewards()` reverts due to invalid getter call.
ground_truth.fix_description: Add `getPoolVote(veTokenId)` in `VoterV3.sol` to return the array. Status: Mitigation confirmed.

vulnerabilities.explanation: The claimRewards() function attempts to call `IVoter(voter).poolVote(veTokenId)` expecting it to return an array of addresses. However, looking at the VoterV3 contract, `poolVote` is defined as a mapping: `mapping(uint256 => address[]) public poolVote`. When accessing a public mapping in Solidity, the auto-generated getter function requires an index parameter and returns a single element, not the entire array. The call `IVoter(voter).poolVote(veTokenId)` would expect a function signature `poolVote(uint256)` that returns `address[]`, but the actual getter signature is `poolVote(uint256, uint256)` returning `address`. This type mismatch will cause the call to revert.
vulnerabilities.attack_scenario: 1. User deposits HYBR and receives gHYBR shares. 2. Operator votes on pools using the vote() function. 3. Time passes and rewards accumulate from bribes and rebases. 4. Operator calls claimRewards() to compound rewards for all gHYBR holders. 5. The function reverts at line 370 when trying to call `IVoter(voter).poolVote(veTokenId)` because the interface expects an array return but the mapping getter doesn't work that way. 6. All accumulated rewards become unclaimable, causing loss of yield for all gHYBR holders.
vulnerabilities.suggested_fix: Add a helper function `getPoolVote(uint256 tokenId)` in VoterV3.sol that returns the entire `poolVote[tokenId]` array: `function getPoolVote(uint256 tokenId) external view returns (address[] memory) { return poolVote[tokenId]; }`. Then update the IVoter interface to include this function and modify claimRewards() to call `IVoter(voter).getPoolVote(veTokenId)` instead of `IVoter(voter).poolVote(veTokenId)`.

prediction.overall_explanation: The GrowthHYBR contract contains a critical logic error in the claimRewards() function. The function incorrectly attempts to access the `poolVote` mapping from the VoterV3 contract as if it were a function returning an array. In Solidity, public mappings with array values generate getter functions that require an additional index parameter and return single elements, not the entire array. This means the claimRewards() function will always revert when called, preventing the operator from claiming any accumulated rewards (rebases and bribes) for the protocol. This effectively breaks the core auto-compounding functionality of the gHYBR token, causing all users to lose their expected yield. The fix requires adding a dedicated getter function in VoterV3 that returns the complete array for a given tokenId.
